videos.title: Real-Time Sensor Data Analytics & AI Implementation with Tiger Cloud
videos.description:
Checkout Tiger Cloud here:-https://fandf.co/3UK4S1P

In this video, we explore how to manage, analyze, and query high-volume time-series data at scale using Tiger Cloud from Tiger Data—powered by PostgreSQL and the TimeScale DB extension.

We set up a managed cloud database via CLI and MCP, execute queries over 1.7 million rows of IoT sensor data, implement automated anomaly detection, optimize performance with hypertables and continuous aggregates, perform columnar data compression, run database forks, and construct a hybrid semantic search engine for AI applications.


Timestamps:
00:00 - Introduction & Real-Time Data Challenges
00:52 - What is Tiger Cloud? (PostgreSQL + TimeScale DB)
02:02 - Overview of the Hands-on Implementation
02:57 - Creating a Compute Service on Tiger Cloud
04:20 - Setting up Tiger CLI & MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server
05:42 - Integrating Tiger Cloud Service with Devon AI Coding Agent
06:47 - Generating 1.7 Million Rows of IoT Sensor Data
07:56 - Applying Optimized Schema, Foreign Keys & Validation Constraints
08:35 - Understanding Hypertables and Automated Partitioning
09:59 - Planting Sensor Faults & Seasonality-Adjusted Anomaly Detection
10:40 - Benchmarking Raw Hypertables vs. Continuous Aggregates
11:31 - Columnar Compression for Historical Data (~70% Storage Reduction)
12:06 - Database Forking & Running Isolated Retention Policies
13:33 - AI Hybrid Search Implementation (EV Station Maintenance Data)
13:46 - Sparse Vector (BM25) vs. Dense Vector (Semantic) Search
14:09 - Generating Vector Embeddings with Local Models & HNSW Indexing
14:46 - Running Hybrid Search Queries using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
15:50 - Summary & Claiming Your $1,000 Free Tiger Cloud Credit

videos.title: Weight Loss Scientist: The Shocking Thing Your Brain Does After You Diet
videos.description:
You lost the weight. Then it came back. There is a reason, and it is not a lack of effort.

In this episode, Giles Yeo and Jay Shetty talk about why losing weight is so hard. Giles is a geneticist and professor at the University of Cambridge who studies how genes shape hunger and body weight, and he explains what your brain does once the weight starts to come off.

He shows why calories are not all equal: your body only uses about 70 of every 100 calories of protein, and a raw stick of celery gives you far fewer calories than the same stick cooked in a stew. He explains why some people can eat more than you and weigh the same, and why your genes can make it harder without meaning you can do nothing about it.

Jay throws Giles some products to judge, and Giles reads the label on a "light" orange juice. They talk about keeping junk food out of your house, how much of your weight is biology, and what happens to your body in middle age.

Learn why the weight you lose fights to come back. And learn the three numbers to watch instead of calories.
